page_title: Deckle — Free paper texture overlay for Mac · Kelvanic

summary.name: Deckle
summary.one_liner: Deckle is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that overlays a subtle procedural paper texture across every app and display.
use_cases: Softening the look of a Mac screen with a matte paper feel
Adding a subtle grain to reduce harsh glow
Applying a warm or tinted texture across all displays
Temporarily disabling the texture with a keyboard shortcut
summary.what_it_does: Deckle runs a transparent window over each display, including the menu bar, that lets clicks, drags and keystrokes pass through to the app beneath. It draws one seamlessly tileable 256-pixel procedural noise texture, repeated across the screen, and offers 18 named textures in colors ranging from neutral gray to amber, plum and graphite. Intensity is adjustable from 5–45%, and each display can be toggled independently. The texture renders once and is cached, and the page states it uses roughly 0% CPU while idle. The app is built in Swift without dependencies and has no Dock icon.
notable: 18 procedural paper textures with adjustable 5–45% intensity
Pass-through transparent overlay window; clicks and keystrokes reach apps underneath
Built in Swift without dependencies; ~0% CPU while idle per the page
Signed and notarized universal build; installable via download or Homebrew
caveats: Page describes it as a visual layer only; no other limitations are stated
